_readme: Single source of truth for every statistic shown on the site. Pages mark numbers with data-stat="key"; scripts/sync_stats.js writes the formatted value into the HTML and tests fail if a page disagrees. Never type a statistic into a page by hand. status: primary = read at the official source; secondary = reported by named outlets, official source not readable by me; derived = computed here from other entries (formula given, recomputed by tests).

ncrb_cases_2021.label: cyber crime cases registered, 2021
ncrb_cases_2021.note: Widely cited NCRB figure; confirmed by a search-engine summary of outlet reports, not read in the NCRB table.

ncrb_cases_2022.label: cyber crime cases registered, 2022
ncrb_cases_2022.note: The NCRB 2022 book exists at this URL (found by search); the figure was confirmed through outlet reports and a search summary.

ncrb_cases_2023.label: cyber crime cases registered, 2023
ncrb_cases_2023.note: Cited by four independent outlets as the 2023 base for the 2024 growth figure.

ncrb_cases_2024.label: cyber crime cases registered, 2024
ncrb_cases_2024.note: Read in four independent write-ups (ETV Bharat, Vajiram, Budding Forensic Expert, Drishti); the NCRB site lists the 2024 report but its tables were not readable.

ncrb_growth_2024_pct.label: growth in cyber crime cases, 2024 over 2023
ncrb_growth_2024_pct.note: Three of four write-ups say 17.9%; one says 17%. Check: 101928/86420 = 1.179.

ncrb_rate_2024.label: cyber crime rate per lakh population, 2024 (6.2 in 2023)

ncrb_fraud_2024.label: cyber crime cases with fraud as the motive, 2024

ncrb_fraud_share_2024_pct.label: share of cyber crime cases that were fraud, 2024

ncrb_telangana_2024.label: cyber crime cases in Telangana, 2024 (highest of any state)

ncrb_karnataka_2024.label: cyber crime cases in Karnataka, 2024 (second highest)
ncrb_karnataka_2024.note: Third place is reported as Maharashtra without a figure in the write-ups read; the full state table was not readable.

ncrp_cases_2024.label: cyber fraud cases recorded, 2024
ncrp_cases_2024.source: MHA reply in Parliament, as reported by ThePrint
ncrp_cases_2024.note: ThePrint attributes the series to an MHA reply to a Lok Sabha question. The reply itself was not read. Other replies give different counts for the same years (definitions differ), so only this set is used.

loss_2024_cr.note: Another analysis of a different reply gives 22,812. This is the figure most outlets report; the site uses one number everywhere.

cfcfrms_saved_cr.label: saved or frozen through CFCFRMS, cumulative, as of 30 June 2026
cfcfrms_saved_cr.source: Rajya Sabha written reply by the MoS Home Affairs (PIB, July 2026), as reported by Sarkaritel and Cyraacs
cfcfrms_saved_cr.note: Two pages state it as more than Rs 11,158 crore across more than 32.80 lakh complaints. PIB itself returned 403. Earlier cumulative figures: 8,189 Cr (31 Dec 2025), 8,690 Cr (31 Jan 2026).

cfcfrms_complaints.label: complaints in which money was saved or frozen, cumulative, as of 30 June 2026

upi_aug2026_bn.label: UPI transactions in August 2026, a record month
upi_aug2026_bn.source: NPCI data, as reported by Medianama and Business Standard
upi_aug2026_bn.note: Worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore; volume up 22% on August 2025. NPCI's own page loads its table by script and could not be read.

mrm_threshold_inr.label: Money Restoration Module: frozen-amount threshold per bank account (a police report is enough up to this level; above it an FIR is compulsory)
mrm_threshold_inr.source: The420.in, and India TV (September 2026) for the process
mrm_threshold_inr.note: Two outlets describe the module; neither gave the portal URL and the I4C page was not readable, so the site points people to cybercrime.gov.in.

rbi_directions.note: Final directions confirmed by a law-firm note and a current-affairs summary; the RBI document itself was not readable. They apply to transactions on or after 1 January 2027, so the compensation below is NOT available for fraud happening today.
